finalOutput:
I wrote the game to `snake_anthropic-claude-opus-5-5_01.html`: one self-contained file of about 700 lines with the HTML, CSS and JavaScript together. I haven't opened it in a browser or run it, so none of the features below have been checked in play.

It's meant to do the following:
- **Grid and rules:** a 30x30 canvas. Each snake moves on its own, grows when it eats food, and dies if it hits a wall, itself or the other snake.
- **Three game modes**, picked from the start menu:
  - Human vs Human: one player uses WASD, the other uses the arrow keys.
  - CPU vs Human: the CPU plays one snake and you play the other.
  - CPU vs CPU: both snakes are computer-controlled.
- **CPU snake:** it finds a path to the food and avoids obstacles. If it can't reach the food, it moves to the safest open neighbouring square.
- **Score:** each snake's score is shown while you play.
- **Screens:** a start menu and a game over screen that shows the winner or a draw.
- **Restart:** press Space or Enter to play again, or Esc to go back to the menu.

To play, open the file in any modern browser.

conversation.contentPreview: Write a snake game in javascript, css, html in one file. Build a classic Snake game on a 30x30 grid. The snake moves continuously in one of four directions and grows when eating food. If it hits a wall or itself, the game ends. Implement keyboard controls for player movement. Add a CPU-controlled snake mode that automatically searches for food. Add the three game modes: human vs human, cpu vs human, cpu vs cpu. Display the score during gameplay. Include a start menu and game over screen. Allow restarting the game with a keypress. Use file name "snake_anthropic-claude-opus-5-5_01.html"

toolCallDetails.arguments:
{"path":"snake_anthropic-claude-opus-5-5_01.html","edit_description":"Create a single-file HTML/CSS/JS Snake game. Requirements:
- Canvas with a 30x30 grid (e.g. 20px cells = 600x600), dark styled page, centered.
- Score bar above canvas showing both snakes' scores (P1 green, P2 blue) and their labels (Human/CPU), plus mode name.
- Start menu overlay: title, 3 mode buttons also selectable by keys 1/2/3: "1 - Human vs Human", "2 - CPU vs Human", "3 - CPU vs CPU". Show controls: Player 1 uses WASD, Player 2 uses Arrow keys. In CPU vs Human, CPU is snake 1 and human is snake 2 using arrows (also allow WASD for that human). P pauses.
- Two snakes, each starting length 3 at opposite sides (snake1 at left moving right, snake2 at right moving left). Continuous movement via fixed tick (~100ms) using setInterval or requestAnimationFrame accumulator. Direction queue per snake (max 2 buffered) preventing 180-degree reversal.
- One food item (maybe 2 foods for two snakes — use 2 foods) placed at random empty cells. Eating grows snake by 1 and +1 score (or +10).
- Collisions: wall, own body, other snake's body -> that snake dies. Head-on head collision -> both die. Game ends when any snake dies; winner = surviving snake, or if both die, higher score wins / draw.
- CPU AI: BFS from head to nearest food avoiding walls and all snake bodies (treat tails as moving—ok to be simple, obstacles = all body segments except tails that will move). If path found take first step, but check safety: after choosing, prefer moves whose reachable flood-fill area >= snake length; if no path, choose the safe neighbor move maximizing flood-fill area. If no safe move, keep direction.
- Game over overlay: shows "Game Over", winner/reason text, final scores, "Press R or Space to restart, M or Esc for menu". R/Space/Enter restarts same mode.
- Draw grid subtle lines, snakes with distinct head color and eyes optional, food as red circles.
- preventDefault for arrow keys and space.
All in one file, clean code."}
